### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db6b4084699f81d63fdb2373720f6973622c9dfe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `899749f6c64b6d9c1a137f5f73217d369d6a83e7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.tsx, docs/adr/0047-object-ui-run-modes.md, docs/adr/README.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.list-view-hide-fields-default-on.ts, packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts, .changeset/29144-interface-toolbar-spec-defaults.md, .changeset/28912-hide-fields-default-on.md, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.relayCensus-11572.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.userActionsSpecDefaults.test.tsx + packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (`UserActionsConfigSchema` L1919–1934), packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts (L1076), ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx (L1867–1872), docs/adr/0047 §3.4, AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13

Judged against the maintainer's ruling on #29144 (comment 6574404727, batch #455, letter A with an ADR-0047 amendment), which this seat wrote and which binds the diff. Read-only review of the committed tree; nothing was built or run here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The four reads match the ruling exactly.** `InterfaceListPage.tsx` L596–599: `filter`, `rowHeight`, `group`, `hideFields` read `!== false`; `search`/`sort` keep `!== false`; `rowColor` keeps `=== true` (spec default `false`, `view.zod.ts` L1932); `allowExport: false` stays. The block is still `cfg.userActions || {}` (L435), so an absent block, an unparsed stored row and a parsed block that omits a key all resolve each on-by-default key to `true`: the ruling's "behave the same" holds by construction, and the new test pins all three routes through the real `PageSchema` (test L115, L136–150). Break attempt: a stored page carrying a serialised `false` from an earlier parse keeps withholding; that is the same residue the #28912 entry already discloses, and the new changeset's "to keep a control closed, write it" is the correct prescription for it. Holds.
- **The spec default is read, not restated.** No second default table is introduced: the page composes booleans from the shared schema's published defaults, and `ListView.tsx` L1867–1872 still reads `ua?.x !== false` for the four, so the page's composed `true`/`false` is the toolbar. The test's "for four blocks the page draws what a list view parses the same block to" (L179, `UserActionsConfigSchema.parse`) is the one-contract pin the ruling asked for. Holds.
- **Reach reading is in the body and matches mine.** 11 showcase pages + HotCRM `account_workbench` declare a block omitting `group`/`hideFields` and already drew both after parse; only block-less and unparsed pages change. My own census on main (12 showcase interface pages, 11 with a block) agrees. Holds.
- **Field security:** the four controls subtract or regroup columns client-side; the objectui#10694 pin (a drawn field the caller may not read is not offered) is in `plugin-list`, untouched. No security-relevant finding; nothing withheld from this record.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29144-interface-toolbar-spec-defaults.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor; `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` at line start in the changeset and the PR body, matching the ruling's claim lines. `semantic` is right: an accepted document's rendered toolbar changes with no change to what parses. The spec grade is `minor` for a prose-only move (entry 18 and the ledger reason), which is what the level axis of `check-changeset-no-major` requires for a `semantic` PR that moves a published package; it over-states the spec change but is the gate's rule, not the diff's error. Right.
- ADR-0087: no D2 conversion is added (none exists for a default read; the parse is unchanged), and no new D3 entry: the behaviour that moves belongs to the #28912 default flip's entry, whose sentence is corrected rather than duplicated. Right — a second entry for the same `hideFields` default would double-announce one change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H** by `docs/adr/0047-object-ui-run-modes.md` and `docs/adr/README.md` (Prime Directive 14): seat ACCEPT + 维护者速读, then the maintainer's own approval and merge. The 速读 is present on the body and names the Tier H ask under 「需要你做的」.
- **ADR-0047 amendment (Prime Directive 13):** a dated 2026-11-02 banner citing the ruling comment id, qualifying TL;DR #1/#5 for the toolbar toggles only, restating §3.4's four closed rows and the export lock; the status line carries the amendment and the README row is regenerated. This is what the ruling bound; the amendment does not rewrite the TL;DR text. Right.
- **Deliberate red: `Check Changeset` (`check-empty-changeset`) fails on this head** because the PR edits the pending `.changeset/28912-hide-fields-default-on.md` it did not add (one bullet, the now-false interface-page sentence). The gate's DELIBERATE CORRECTION class; the correction is named in the claim amendment (6574419950) and the PR body. For the maintainer: approving this PR also accepts that red. For the seat: if `Check Changeset` is a required check for the merge queue, the landing path (maintainer merge by hand vs enqueue) must be one the red does not block; say which in the ACCEPT record.
- Spec `check:generated` is reported up to date on the head, so entry 18 is hand-written text, not a regenerated artifact; the ruling's "regenerated in the spec regen order" is satisfied vacuously.

### ④ Design judgment

**`InterfaceListPage.tsx`** — judged against the ruling and `view.zod.ts`.
- The rewritten comment (L579–592) states the mechanism and the defect (a control drawn only after a parse materialised the default) and anchors ADR-0047 as amended, so the ADR id stays in the code (Prime Directive 13 corollary). The header docblock (L17–19) no longer promises "absent by default". Holds.
- The relay-census reasons for `userActions` and `compactToolbar` drop "closed by default" and name the `false` opt-out and `rowColor` opt-in; the census test stays a true description of the page. Holds.

**`docs/adr/0047-object-ui-run-modes.md`** — judged against §3.4 and the ruling.
- The banner's list (search, sort, filter, rowHeight, group, hideFields on; rowColor off) is exactly the set the page reads, no more; it does not speak for keys the page does not read (`refresh`, `addRecordForm`, `editInline`), which is right since the page reads `editInline` elsewhere under its own entry. Every closed item it restates is a §3.4 row or the page's `allowExport: false`. Holds.

**`18.list-view-hide-fields-default-on.ts` / `default-changes.ts` / `.changeset/28912-…`** — judged against the consumer code they describe.
- All three now say the page reads the same default and `hideFields: false` withholds; each is true on this head (`InterfaceListPage.tsx` L599). The ledger reason also says the page "does the same for `filter`, `rowHeight` and `group`", true on this head (L596–598). The prescription an upgrading deployment needs (write `false` to withhold) is unchanged and correct on both surfaces. Holds.

**`InterfaceListPage.userActionsSpecDefaults.test.tsx`** — 17 cases; mocks `ListView` to capture the composed schema, so it pins the page's contribution and not plugin-list's; the ablation (hideFields back to `=== true`) reds 8 of 17 with the parsed-`{}` case staying green, which is precisely the defect's signature. Holds.

No must-fix found. No should-fix. One landing note under ③ (the deliberate red and the queue).

**席位意见**：建议批准。改动与裁决 A 逐条对应，代码只动一处映射，其余是文档和说明文字的同步改正；改正 28912 那句是必要的，不改就会发布一句已经不对的说明。
